description: An original, jurisdiction-neutral elevator scheduled preventive maintenance service record for a passenger or service conveyance whose doors, leveling, controls, machine spaces, communications, inspection status, and operating restrictions require qualified review. It connects facility identity, asset-specific evidence, hazards, qualified decisions, exceptions, service status, and accountable closeout without replacing employer procedures or trade judgment.

blocks.label: Record reference and timing
Facility, location, and responsible parties

blocks.guidance: This Elevator record organizes facts and evidence. It does not replace employer energy-control procedures, permits, manufacturer instructions, required inspection, emergency response, or qualified trade judgment. Stop and route any unsafe or uncertain condition.
blocks.label: Safety and authority boundary

sections.guidance: Open one traceable record, identify the responsible parties, and set the review route.
sections.title: Elevator Preventive Maintenance identity and routing

blocks.label: Elevator asset and system profile

blocks.guidance: Check only directly observed or source-supported items; explain inaccessible, not applicable, or conflicting evidence below.
items: Car, controller, machine, disconnect, and building identifiers reconcile
Landing and car doors, gates, interlocks, sills, and closing behavior are recorded
Leveling, starting, stopping, ride quality, noise, and vibration observations are captured
Car operating panel, indicators, call stations, and floor signals are documented
Alarm, two-way communication, emergency lighting, and recall status are recorded
Machine room, control space, pit, hoistway access, keys, and barriers are controlled
Brake, governor, ropes, belts, sheaves, hydraulic equipment, or buffers are referenced
Water intrusion, oil leakage, debris, heat, odor, and housekeeping conditions are recorded
Controller faults, callbacks, entrapments, shutdowns, and repeated symptoms are linked
Required inspection, test, certificate, permit, and maintenance-control records are referenced
Jumpers, bypasses, out-of-service controls, and temporary restrictions are visible
Work is limited to qualified conveyance personnel and the authorized scope

blocks.guidance: Tie each entry to a location, source, reading condition, photo, tag, log, or other retrievable evidence.

Every task records completed, not applicable, deferred, or failed status
Settings and adjustments preserve before value, after value, and authority
Parts, materials, consumables, lot or serial data, and waste route are traceable
Functional tests record conditions, acceptance source, result, and reviewer
Deferred work remains open with risk, restriction, owner, due point, and escalation

blocks.guidance: A checked condition requires immediate protective action, a named owner, qualified review, and a final disposition.
items: Entrapment, uncontrolled movement, unintended door motion, or unsafe leveling is reported
Door interlock, gate, brake, governor, recall, alarm, or communication function may be impaired
Water, smoke, fire, oil, debris, or electrical condition affects the car, pit, hoistway, or controls
Required isolation, access control, barricade, key control, or qualified personnel is absent
An unauthorized jumper, bypass, reset, or return-to-service request is identified
Exposed energized parts, moving equipment, suspended load, or stored energy is uncontrolled
Certificate, inspection, test, permit, shutdown, or authority restriction is unresolved
Observed condition conflicts with controller logs, callback history, inspection evidence, or field status

blocks.guidance: Do not resolve a checked stop condition by inference, an unchecked box, or a generic sign-off. Preserve the condition, protective action, authority, evidence, owner, due point, and verified disposition.

blocks.guidance: Check only controls supported by referenced evidence; unresolved controls remain open conditions.
items: All planned tasks have evidence or an explicit deferred disposition
Parts, settings, fluids, materials, and configuration changes are reconciled
Required operational and protective-device checks have accepted results
Open defects have risk controls, owners, due points, and communication
Next interval reflects condition, runtime, environment, and governing plan
Qualified reviewer separately approves return-to-service evidence
Qualified elevator personnel control testing, adjustment, repair, and return to service
Door, leveling, brake, governor, recall, alarm, and communication evidence is reconciled
Any out-of-service or restricted condition has barriers, notices, and an accountable owner
Controller resets or cleared faults are not accepted without cause and verification evidence
Required authority, inspection, certificate, and maintenance-control records are current
Building operations approve occupant communication and alternate-access arrangements

items: Car and landing access status, barriers, keys, and notices match the final disposition

Controller logs, service notes, test evidence, and authority records are filed
